major: MAJ-1 (residual of F1-4; the CLAUDE.md row and the PR body describe a tie-break the bytes do not produce). In the view, the card and the prune, the key (list_vs_sale = 'sale') DESC comes AFTER captured_at DESC. So the sale wins only when last_seen AND captured_at both tie. The row tells S81-17 to write a list and a sale price as two rows of one observation, and a changed amount is a new row with a later captured_at. Under that contract, when a LIST price changes during an ongoing sale, the new list row ranks first at every later observation that sees both rows. Measured on PostgreSQL 18.1 (probe S-b, rolled back): sale 30 first seen 2026-10-10 and list 55 (new row, captured 2026-10-18), both last_seen 2026-10-20. The view and kb_product_card both serve list 55, and kb_prune_offers(1, 1) deletes the still-observed sale row. Three sentences are false in that case. (1) CLAUDE.md S81-14 row, Offers bullet: '(a sale row ranks before a list row observed at the same instant: the sale is what the shopper pays; S81-17's ingest writes a list and a sale price as two rows of one observation)'. (2) PR body, What lands: 'a sale row beats a list row of the same instant'. (3) PR body stated limit 17: 'A sale and a list row of one observation tie-break to the sale'. Two texts are true as written: the 045 header ('of the same last_seen and captured_at') and F1-4's literal key order. 045 is not applied yet, so either fix is cheap now. (a) A ruling that moves the key ahead of captured_at in the view, the card and the prune, with OFFER_ORDER / VIEW_TEXT / CARD_TEXT / HEADER_OFFERS / the POSTCHECK tie-break re-pinned and an S-b row added. (b) Rewrite the row and PR sentences to the header's exact condition, state the S-b outcome as a limit, and give S81-17 / S81-18 a contract: the reader picks the sale within one observation, or the writer re-captures the sale row when the list amount changes.
minor: m1 (V4 survived; pin gap in F1-3): a bool Source field (is_shopify / is_render_only / is_algolia / requires_super) that accepts an int survives the whole file, because registry_bool_field_type tests only the string 'yes'. One refusal row with is_shopify: 1 kills it.

m2 (V6 survived; pin gap in F1-3): the domain == host check is pinned only against a domain with a different registrable name (other.example; noon.com on shop.example). A 'last two labels equal' mutant survives, so a sibling-subdomain entry would pass, for example om.swissarabian.com on ksa.swissarabian.com (the M13-12 class, with real rows in the registry). One refusal row (host ksa.shop.example, domain om.shop.example) kills it.

m3 (F1-6 completeness): the stated reason for refusing all-digit hosts is 'a WHATWG parser reads a numeric last label as IPv4'. That rule also covers a 0x-hex last label, and glibc inet_aton reads 127.0.0.0x1 as 127.0.0.1. Such hosts pass the leaf: canonical_offer_url returns http://127.0.0.0x1/p, http://0x7f.0x0.0x0.0x1/p and http://1.2.3.0x4/p unchanged, and the merchant and image builders accept them. They also pass the 045 kb_merchants_host_top_label_letter CHECK; PG probe S-c inserted the merchant and an offer on 127.0.0.0x1. Incomplete as written: the row's 'canonical_offer_url ... refuses ... an IP literal', the comment on KB_HOST_TOP_LABEL_REGEX, and PR stated limit 18. Fix: refuse a last label matching ^(0x[0-9a-f]*|[0-9]+)$ in the leaf and the constraint, or state the limit. Impact today is a stored, user-facing loopback link (every server fetch path goes through url_validator).

m4 (next to F1-1, outside the R-A5 text): a placeholder BRAND still mints an id under a placeholder brand axis. Measured: (Unknown, Sauvage) -> fragrances|unknown|sauvage|-, (N/A, Sauvage) -> fragrances|a+n|sauvage|-, (Unknown Brand, Sauvage) -> fragrances|brand+unknown|sauvage|-, (Product, Sauvage) -> fragrances|product|sauvage|-. So 'brand unknown, name X' scans from different houses share one juice id per name. Either record it as a writer contract (S81-16 / S81-17 never pass a placeholder brand) or extend the rule with is_placeholder_identity(brand).

m5 (F1-11 wording): the row, the leaf docstring and the PR body say 'its own code does no I/O ... no env read'. But the function-local 'from app.services import source_router' in _registry_ok runs source_router's module body on the first merchant build. That body reads ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES, reads data/bh_gcc_sources.json when the flag is ON (ON in production), and imports search_descriptor_service. The import-hazard sentence names only the dotenv path; one more clause would complete it.

m6 (previous round's correctness m13: neither closed nor recorded): kb_feedback has no index leading on compare_request_id, and S81-22's deletion hook will filter on that column. RULINGS_FIX1, the CLAUDE.md row and the PR body do not mention it. Record it for S81-22's 048, or add the index to 045 before apply.

m7 (PR body count): 'the eleven belt-only rows' is wrong. The diff re-points NINE deny rows: offers url_denied; images url_denied, provenance_denied, provenance_denied_sub; specs source_denied; reviews source_url_denied; gaps hint_denied_host, hint_denied_url, hint_denied_name. That makes 14 re-pointed rows with the five named before it, while the fix report says 15.

m8 (noted for readers; stated by the ruling): only kb_merchants.host carries the top-label CHECK. Offers inherit it through the merchant FK plus url_on_merchant. The other data tables' URL and host columns have no such CHECK: SQL stored an image with provenance_host 10.0.0.1 and url https://10.0.0.1/i.jpg (measured; the leaf refuses both). The 045 header's 'Every host carries a letter in its top-level label' sits in the kb_merchants paragraph and is true there.
